skill.name: react-patterns

skill.summary: Apply modern React patterns for maintainable components, hooks, state, performance, and TypeScript.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in this prompt-only skill. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or instructions to bypass security review in SKILL.md. No remediation is required.

content.value_statement: React teams need consistent patterns for components, hooks, state, performance, and testing. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise guidance for production React decisions.
actual_capabilities: Explains component roles and responsibility boundaries.
Recommends hook extraction rules and effect cleanup practices.
Maps state complexity to useState, Context, React Query, Zustand, or Redux Toolkit.
Summarizes React 19 hooks and compiler guidance.
Prioritizes performance profiling, memoization, virtualization, and stable callbacks.
Covers TypeScript, testing, accessibility, and anti-pattern guidance.
limitations: Does not include executable automation or project-specific code generation.
Does not inspect a repository unless the user provides files.
Does not replace framework documentation for exact API behavior.
Does not cover non-React frontend frameworks in depth.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Component Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a React component for [feature]. Recommend component boundaries, state placement, and props.

prompt_templates.title: Extract a Custom Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repeated React logic and suggest whether it should become a custom hook. Explain the hook API and cleanup needs.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Performance Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this React view for avoidable re-renders. Prioritize profiling steps, virtualization, memoization, and callback stability.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a React 19 Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a React 19 approach for [app area]. Include server and client boundaries, form actions, optimistic updates, TypeScript types, tests, and error recovery.

output_examples.input: A developer asks where to store filter state for a product list.
output: Keep filter state in the list feature when only that route uses it.
Lift it to a parent when sibling controls need the same value.
Use URL state when filters must be shareable or restorable.

output_examples.input: A team wants to optimize a slow React table.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends profiling first, then virtualizing large rows, memoizing expensive derived values, and avoiding broad context updates.

output_examples.input: A form needs modern React 19 behavior.
output: Use action state for submission feedback.
Use optimistic updates when the user should see immediate progress.
Add error recovery that protects entered user data.

best_practices: Start with small components that have one responsibility.
Place state at the narrowest scope that still supports the user flow.
Profile before adding memoization or callback stabilization.
anti_patterns: Using useEffect for derived values that belong in render or server data.
Introducing global state before local or feature-level state is insufficient.
Optimizing every component before measuring user-visible slowdowns.

faq.question: Does this skill write React code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides React design guidance that an AI assistant can apply when planning or reviewing code.

faq.question: Which React topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers component design, hooks, state selection, React 19 patterns, composition, performance, errors, TypeScript, and testing.

faq.question: Can it help with performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends profiling first, then targeted fixes such as virtualization, memoization, and stable callbacks.

faq.question: Is this useful for TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for props, reusable component types, children, events, and refs.

faq.question: Does it require network or file access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a prompt document and does not include executable scripts or network behavior.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Frontend engineers, technical leads, and developers using Claude, Codex, or Claude Code for React work.
